hypothesis: H-LBINV: the organizer metric inverts. With alpha=0.2, beta=0.8 the distance-weighted Tversky index collapses for binary predictions to DTI = TP/(0.2*D + 0.8*N), whose denominator contains no TP term, so each published raster's leaderboard score is a linear measurement of the hidden truth set. Solving the 128x128 normal equations in the file-by-file dot-incidence space recovers a per-cell credit field q; dots are emitted where q > 0.2*DTI.
mechanism: Least-norm solution of (O + lambda*I) alpha = t with O the 128x128 pairwise dot-overlap Gram matrix and t_i = s_i*(0.2*D_i + 0.8*N); u(x) = sum_i alpha_i 1[x in P_i]; q = clip(c*u, 0, 1). c and N are fitted by leave-one-file-out error on the same 128 files (LOO RMSE 0.0533, rho 0.757 vs predict-the-mean baseline 0.0825). Dots emitted by the metric's own marginal rule q > 0.2*DTI, spaced >=2 px, then repaired to the literal 65% uniqueness cap by dropping the lowest-q offenders.
mimic: Non-fault linear artefacts that the published dot patterns also cover: basin-margin relief, drainage alignment, and survey-line striping. Because q is a weighted sum of published dot patterns, it inherits their false-positive structure; the field redistributes existing recall rather than creating new one.

holdout_dti.note: The leaderboard-inversion estimator is validated by leave-one-file-out over the 128 published rasters (RMSE 0.0533, rho 0.757), not by a catalogue hide-and-recover holdout. A catalogue holdout is anti-concordant with the real leaderboard (rho +0.143, n=21) because known USGS/INGENIOUS fault pixels are masked out of scoring. No HOLDOUT-DTI is reported for this file.

leakage_canary.note: The field q is derived from published dot patterns, not from the label raster. A single-feature canary on the raw geophysical bands was run in the prior session (worst symmetric AUC 0.90, evidence/leakage_canary_report.json).
